result.summary: This PR adds functional test coverage for the case where the miner cannot satisfy timestamp constraints (MTP at the future-time limit), checking both getblocktemplate RPC and the IPC mining interface, and confirming the IPC connection survives the failure and recovers a second later. It also includes preparatory refactor commits that rename and consolidate duplicated block-timing constants (REGTEST_N_BITS, REGTEST_TARGET, DIFFICULTY_ADJUSTMENT_INTERVAL, HALVING_INTERVAL) across several test files, and a small follow-up assertion for Murch-Zawy period boundaries suggested during #35949 review.
result.problem: There was no test coverage for the (impractical but reachable) scenario where template construction fails because the minimum allowed block time exceeds the future-time limit, and it was unclear whether the newly added timewarp/Murch-Zawy miner rules interacted with this pre-existing edge case. Reviewers and the author wanted this clarified and documented rather than left as an unverified assumption.

fjahr noted the final version mines ~450 blocks across three rounds to illustrate different retarget-period positions, which feels heavy for the edge case being tested, but explicitly said this is not a blocker

result.card: This PR adds functional test coverage for an edge case where getblocktemplate and the IPC mining interface both fail to produce a block template because minimum-time and future-time constraints conflict, and verifies the IPC connection survives the failure and recovers a second later. It clarifies, per author Sjors, that this pre-existing 'impractical' issue is unaffected by the recently merged timewarp-protection and Murch-Zawy miner rules (#30681, #35949), resolving confusion raised during that review. It also includes small refactor commits consolidating duplicated block-timing constants across mining_basic.py, rpc_blockchain.py, and blocktools.py. Reviewer fjahr moved from concept-ACK-with-questions to a full code review ACK on the final version, with one nonblocking nit that the test mines more blocks (~450) than strictly needed for the scenario. The PR has no open blocking objections and no stated dependency on another PR.
